title: Hexed Review: Disney's Bold but Familiar Magical Fantasy
excerpt:
Disney's animated feature explores teenage identity through witchcraft.
A review praises its characters but questions its reliance on familiar fantasy imagery.
body_md:
Billie Doe is an Ohio teenager whose unusual abilities have troubled her protective mother, Alice, since childhood. A mysterious bracelet is connected to her powers, and removing it opens a gateway to Hexe, a sanctuary for witches that turns out to be divided under Queen Celeste's rule.

The review finds particular value in the use of witchcraft as a metaphor for adolescent alienation. Billie's gothic appearance and uneasy relationship with her mother give the fantasy an emotional foundation. The relationship between Billie, Alice and the queen provides an interesting dramatic dynamic.

Hailee Steinfeld and Rashida Jones voice the daughter and mother, with Jodie Foster playing Celeste and Walton Goggins portraying a three-eyed cat. The reviewer singles out Goggins as a welcome calming presence amid the hectic action.

The reservations concern originality and pacing. The magical city and several narrative elements recall Wicked so closely that the reviewer considers the similarities more than simple homage. Some sequences also outstay their welcome, although parts of the world-building evoke the appeal of Zootopia.

Directed by Fawn Veerasunthorn and Jason Hand, the 103-minute film represents a bolder approach than Wish in this critic's assessment. Its themes and characters offer promise, but the review argues that the execution needs more original inspiration. This is an individual critical assessment rather than a consensus.
